v1-phi-c-certainty.qualification: Translation by Denis Paul and G. E. M. Anscombe; edited by G. E. M. Anscombe and G. H. von Wright.

v1-phi-c-consciousness.locator: Table 1, Figure 3 and Box 1 in the accepted manuscript.
v1-phi-c-consciousness.qualification: The working picture in the text is an orientation; it does not settle how physical activity becomes felt experience.

v1-phi-c-memory.qualification: The compression metaphor and the assessment of this particular memory belong to the author.

v1-phi-c-registration.locator: Abstract and discussion of measurement correlations and environmental interaction.
v1-phi-c-registration.qualification: Extending registration into an ancestry of human experience is the author’s philosophical proposal, not a result of this paper.

v1-phi-c-language.qualification: The qualification on meaning-as-use matters; the text is paraphrased, not quoted from a named English translation.

v1-phi-c-institutions.qualification: The operating-system image and its proposed inversion are the author’s extensions.

v1-phi-c-gettier.qualification: The stopped clock is a familiar illustration of epistemic luck, not one of Gettier’s two cases in this paper.

v1-phi-c-hume.locator: Section IV, Part II; compare Section V, Part I.

v1-phi-c-certainty-background.qualification: The practical recommendation about revisability is the author’s reading.

v1-phi-c-validity.locator: Aristotle, Book I, chapters 1 and 4; Lehman, Leighton and Meyer, §1.4.1.
v1-phi-c-validity.qualification: The basket examples are illustrative constructions. Modern validity concerns truth preservation; true premises are a further requirement for a sound argument.

v1-phi-c-empty.qualification: An empty set is not identified with a physical vacuum or the philosophical absence of existence.

v1-phi-c-null.qualification: The example concerns SQL’s missing-value treatment, not a universal meaning of null across programming languages.

v1-phi-c-russell.qualification: The paradox concerns unrestricted set formation; contemporary set theories restrict it.

v1-phi-c-hilbert.locator: Hilbert, Problem 2; Whitehead and Russell, Volume I; Russell, Appendix A on Frege.
v1-phi-c-hilbert.qualification: Hilbert’s consistency programme and the logicist projects are related but distinct. The English Hilbert text translates the 1900 address.

v1-phi-c-godel.locator: Feferman, pp. 4–9; Gödel, Propositions VI and XI.
v1-phi-c-godel.qualification: The first result is stated in its modern Gödel–Rosser form. The interlude distinguishes the original consistency assumptions.

v1-phi-c-godel-extension.qualification: A stronger consistent, effective arithmetical theory can settle additional statements while remaining incomplete; no theorem about civil society follows automatically.

v1-phi-c-companions.qualification: Mag/Maggie and Al/Alexander are literary associations. Pearl and protector are not the chemical elements’ etymologies.

v1-phi-i-sets.qualification: The cardinalities of ∅ and {∅} are respectively zero and one.

v1-phi-i-null.qualification: Ordinary comparisons involving NULL and the dedicated IS NULL predicate perform different operations.

v1-phi-i-structure.qualification: The friendship example is the author’s illustration of the modelling choice, not an empirical finding about friendship.

v1-phi-i-logic.locator: §1.4.1, modus ponens and sound inference rules.
v1-phi-i-logic.qualification: The alarm example contrasts modus ponens with the invalid converse inference known as affirming the consequent.

v1-phi-i-calculus.qualification: The prose specifies differentiability and one-dimensional motion; integrating velocity requires an initial position to recover a particular position history.

v1-phi-i-godel-coding.locator: §§1–2 and Proposition VI, in B. Meltzer’s English translation.
v1-phi-i-godel-coding.qualification: The self-reference concerns formal provability, not the liar paradox.

v1-phi-i-rosser.locator: Opening statement of the strengthening from omega-consistency to ordinary consistency.
v1-phi-i-rosser.qualification: The terminology in the prose is modernized; the result still requires an effective theory of sufficient arithmetical strength.

v1-phi-i-godel-consistency.qualification: The claim concerns the theory’s standard formal representation of its own consistency under the theorem’s conditions.

v1-phi-i-halting.qualification: The draft uses the modern halting presentation of diagonalization, rather than reproducing Turing’s circle-free-machine argument verbatim.

v1-phi-i-metrology.qualification: The thermometer and room examples are hypothetical. Repeated readings alone need not reveal a shared systematic offset.

v1-phi-i-decoherence.qualification: Decoherence and the interpretation of definite outcomes are distinguished; no consciousness-induced collapse is asserted.

v1-phi-i-quantum-records.locator: Discussion of measurement, environmental monitoring and stable correlations.
v1-phi-i-quantum-records.qualification: The text does not assert a unique settled quantum/classical boundary or equate a physical record with subjective experience.

v1-phi-i-popper.locator: Chapter 1, section I, especially numbered conclusions 1–7.
v1-phi-i-popper.qualification: The linked essay excerpt predates its inclusion in the 1963 collection. Falsifiability is presented as one influential account of scientific testing.

v1-phi-i-duhem.qualification: The material-under-load illustration is the author’s application of the argument, not Duhem’s example.

v1-phi-i-reproduction.qualification: Following this report’s usage: reproducibility concerns results from the same data and computational procedures; replication uses newly collected data. Usage varies by field.

v1-phi-i-bayes.qualification: The detector example is invented: 100 × 0.90 = 90 true alarms; 9,900 × 0.05 = 495 false alarms; 90/585 ≈ 15.38%. The modern update description is not a quotation from Bayes.

v1-phi-i-switching.qualification: The switch illustration takes conduction as true. Shannon’s original hindrance notation uses zero for a closed circuit and one for an open one.

v1-phi-i-learning-proof.locator: AlphaProof: a formal approach to reasoning.
v1-phi-i-learning-proof.qualification: This is the research team’s report about a particular system, not a claim that all learned systems supply proofs or that a proof establishes general understanding.
